reasons: target_missing: a play names a card whose printed effects aim at ONE enemy and carries no target, so the line cannot be replayed at all

forecast_missing: the board registered questions to be answered BEFORE the line and the form carries no answer, or fewer answers than questions -- a forecast collected after the line is a rationalisation

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I spent 3 Sparks with Bag of Tricks to place three Bombs, then played Mine Toss on Shrinker Beetle to place another Bomb, then played Run Away! for 4 Block. My forecasts were: 0 Spark at the end of this turn, 4 Spark at the start of next turn, and 25 damage dealt by then.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered adding Spirited Away after Mine Toss for 12 more Block, using the remaining 2 Energy.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up 12 additional Block from Spirited Away, preserving no benefit from the remaining 2 Energy against the displayed debuff intent.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. A sufficiently large attack intent would have made me add Spirited Away after Mine Toss, while retaining the same Bomb setup and Run Away!.

survives_means: not yet falsified -- this funnel refuses turns and never rates them

findings.why: play 1 names 'Bag of Tricks', whose printed effects aim at ONE enemy, and carries no target. The bridge has nothing to aim at, so this line cannot be replayed -- it is sealed and UNTESTED, which is the state KLEESPARK-R1 ended two of its eight lines in

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
targets.repair: out of scope by M63: this refuses a form and never repairs one

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
